Background/Objective Despite multiple attempts, no surrogate biomarker of Parkinson disease (PD) has been definitively identified. Alternatively, identifying a non-invasive biomarker is crucial to understanding the natural history, severity, and progression of PD and to guide future therapeutic trials. Recent work highlighted alpha synuclein-containing extracellular vesicles and Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP-1) activity as drivers of PD pathogenesis and putative PD biomarkers. This exploratory study evaluated the role of alpha-synuclein-positive extracellular vesicles and PARP-1 activity in the plasma of PD patients as non-invasive markers of the disease’s severity and progression. Methods We collected plasma of 57 PD patients (discovery cohort 20, replication cohort 37) and compared it with 20 unaffected individuals, 20 individuals with clinically diagnosed Alzheimer’s disease, and 20 individuals with dementia with Lewy bodies. We analyzed alpha-synuclein-positive extracellular vesicles from platelet-free plasma by nanoscale flow cytometry and blood concentrations of poly ADP-ribose using sandwich ELISA kits. Results Median concentration of α-synuclein extracellular vesicles was significantly higher in PD patients compared to the other groups (Kruskal-Wallis, p < .0001). In the discovery cohort, patients with higher α-synuclein extracellular vesicles had a higher Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale score (UPDRS III median = 22 vs. 5, p = 0.045). Seven out of 20 patients (35%) showed detectable PAR levels, with positive patients showing significantly higher levels of α-synuclein extracellular vesicles. In the replication cohort, we did not observe a significant difference in the PAR-positive cases in relationship with UPDRS III. Conclusions Non-invasive determination of α-synuclein-positive extracellular vesicles may provide a potential non-invasive marker of PD disease severity, and longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate the role of α-synuclein-positive extracellular vesicles as a marker of disease progression. extracted_data.document_summary: This exploratory study investigated α-synuclein-positive extracellular vesicles (α-synuclein-EVs) and poly (ADP-ribose) (PAR) levels in the plasma of Parkinson disease (PD) patients. The aim was to evaluate these as non-invasive biomarkers for PD diagnosis, severity, and progression, comparing PD patients to unaffected controls, Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Key findings showed significantly higher α-synuclein-EV levels in PD patients, which could distinguish them from controls and other neurodegenerative diseases. Detectable PAR plasma levels were associated with higher α-synuclein-EV levels in PD patients, suggesting a PARP-1/α-synuclein cross-talk in systemic circulation. The study also determined that α-synuclein-EVs do not primarily originate from red blood cells. While α-synuclein-EVs showed potential as a diagnostic marker and an initial correlation with disease severity (UPDRS scores) in a discovery cohort, this correlation was not consistently replicated in the larger cohort, indicating that single timepoint levels may not reliably predict disease severity. Longitudinal studies are suggested to evaluate their role as markers of disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker identification, assessment, and characterization for Parkinson Disease (PD) and related neurodegenerative conditions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study focused on biomarker analysis, not a therapeutic intervention. Plasma samples were collected from 57 PD patients (discovery cohort 20, replication cohort 37), 20 unaffected individuals, 20 Alzheimer's disease patients, and 20 dementia with Lewy bodies patients. All cohorts were age/sex matched. α-synuclein extracellular vesicles were quantified from platelet-free/poor plasma using nanoscale flow cytometry, and poly ADP-ribose levels were determined using sandwich ELISA kits. No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic intervention were conducted or reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Platelet-free/poor plasma; EVs isolated from blood
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (on extracellular vesicles, quantified by nanoscale-flow cytometry and detectability by Western blot)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median α-synuclein EV concentration was significantly higher in PD patients (138,867 EVs/µl, range 10,173–2,758,267) compared to unaffected individuals (13,253 EVs/µl), Alzheimer's disease (11,603 EVs/µl), and dementia with Lewy bodies (12,393 EVs/µl) groups (Kruskal-Wallis, p < .0001). In the discovery cohort, patients with higher α-synuclein EVs had higher UPDRS III scores (median = 22 vs. 5, p = 0.045), although this correlation was not replicated in the larger cohort, suggesting single timepoint levels may not consistently predict disease severity. Higher α-synuclein-EV levels were also significantly associated with detectable Poly (ADP-ribose) (PAR) levels in PD patients (p = 0.048).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: α-synuclein is a protein central to Parkinson's disease pathogenesis, forming aggregates and associated with intracellular toxicity. Its presence in extracellular vesicles reflects disease processes, intercellular communication, and a possible mechanism for cell-to-cell spreading of abnormal fibrillary α-synucleins, contributing to synucleinopathy pathophysiology.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis and differentiation of Parkinson's disease from unaffected controls, Alzheimer's disease dementia, and Lewy body dementia, particularly in the context of cell-to-cell transmission of α-synuclein aggregates and impaired autophagy in PD.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential non-invasive marker for PD diagnosis (AUC = 0.929, sensitivity 92.98%, specificity 78.95% at cut-off 20,700 EVs/µl) and for identifying specific disease subtypes. While initially linked to disease severity (UPDRS scores) in a discovery cohort, this correlation was not replicated consistently. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate its role as a marker of disease progression.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Product Concentration (reflecting PARP-1 activity, determined by sandwich ELISA kit)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Seven out of 20 patients (35%) showed detectable PAR levels in plasma, with positive patients having significantly higher levels of α-synuclein extracellular vesicles (median 59,800 EVs/µl vs 23,347 EVs/µl in PAR- patients, p = 0.048). For PAR+ patients, median plasma concentration was 255 pM (range 0.038–613). Higher levels were also observed in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of PD patients compared to healthy donors. No significant difference in PAR-positive cases in relationship with UPDRS III was observed in the replication cohort, and no overall correlation with disease severity (UPDRS scores) was found.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Product of PARP-1 activity. PARP-1 is a fundamental component of DNA damage-response machinery, utilizing NAD+ and ATP. Hyper-activated PARP-1 leads to regulated cell death (parthanatos) and is implicated as a driver of PD pathogenesis by accelerating α-synuclein propagation and neuronal cell death, potentially secondary to excessive nitric oxide production from Lewy Body accumulation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Parkinson disease diagnosis and pathogenesis, specifically in blood plasma and CSF, where detectable PAR levels correlate with α-synuclein-positive EV levels. Relevant in neurotoxicity linked to excessive PARP-1 activation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Putative PD biomarker, reflecting PARP-1 activity and potentially identifying a subtype of PD. Detectability and higher levels are associated with higher α-synuclein-EV levels in PD patients. Inconsistent correlation with disease severity (UPDRS III). PARP inhibitors may represent a future adjuvant neuroprotective approach.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median RBC-EV concentration was 6,593 EVs/µl (range 1,200–26,827) in the PD group, significantly higher compared to AD dementia and DLB groups (p = 0.059). Unaffected controls (CU): 2,910 EVs/µl (range 1,200–6,453); AD dementia: 4,017 EVs/µl (range 0–10,340); DLB: 3,480 EVs/µl (range 480–13,340).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Extracellular vesicles derived from red blood cells are involved in intercellular communication and reflect the state of red blood cells. Investigated to understand the origin of α-synuclein EVs.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis of Parkinson's disease from AD dementia and DLB, specifically when investigating the origin of plasma-derived α-synuclein-EVs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated concentration in PD patients compared to AD and DLB. However, analysis of α-synuclein+CD235a+ EVs indicated that peripheral α-synuclein EVs do not primarily originate from RBCs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The percentage of α-synuclein+CD235a+ EVs did not differ significantly between groups. Median percentage was 0.76% (CU), 0.87% (AD), 0.80% (DLB), and 0.604% (PD).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: CD235a is a marker for red blood cells. This combined marker indicates α-synuclein EVs originating from red blood cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Determining the origin of circulating α-synuclein EVs in Parkinson's disease patients and controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant difference across groups suggests that peripheral α-synuclein EVs do not primarily originate from red blood cells.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detectable in 4 out of 5 samples from PD patients. Not detected in healthy donors (N=3). No observed difference between total α-synuclein and α-synuclein phosphoS129 in PD patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Total α-synuclein is a key protein in the pathology of Parkinson's disease and other synucleinopathies.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Validation of α-synuclein presence in EVs from PD patients compared to healthy individuals.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Presence in peripheral EVs is associated with Parkinson's disease.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detectable in 4 out of 5 samples from PD patients. Not detected in healthy donors (N=3). No observed difference between total α-synuclein and α-synuclein phosphoS129 in PD patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Phosphorylation of α-synuclein at Serine 129 is a significant post-translational modification associated with α-synuclein aggregation and toxicity in synucleinopathies.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Validation of phosphorylated α-synuclein presence in EVs from PD patients compared to healthy individuals.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Presence in peripheral EVs is associated with Parkinson's disease.
